clue.text: US city's generous daily medical insurance?

definitions.note: the possessive reads as 'US city is', the 's working as a link

parts.note: a big portion is a generous one
an apple a day keeps the doctor away, so one apple daily insures against needing medical care

explanation.surface: A question about some generous health cover taken out every day by a city's residents.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful definition: the proverb 'an apple a day keeps the doctor away' makes the fruit a kind of daily health insurance.
explanation.definitionFit: New York is nicknamed after a large piece of fruit, the long-standing tag for that great American metropolis.

clue.text: Bold sort of lead a bishop brought in occupied primate

indicators.note: the pieces are placed inside the word for occupied

parts.note: busy means occupied or engaged
HB, hard black, is a grade of pencil lead
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bold kind of leadership in which a bishop is brought into a busy primate's world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primate' could be an archbishop beside the bishop; it is a small African animal. HB is a pencil-lead grade.
explanation.definitionFit: A bushbaby is a small nocturnal African primate, also called a galago.

clue.text: Good for everyone to have convict in prison system

parts.note: U is the British film certificate meaning universal, suitable for all
a lag is an old convict, as in old lag

explanation.surface: It's good for all of us that a convict is held inside the prison system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for everyone' is the U film rating in Britain, open to all audiences.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gulag was the Soviet network of forced-labour camps, a notorious penal system.

clue.text: Expert horseman in team, I am rising star

parts.note: a pro is a professional, an expert

indicators.note: the other pieces sit inside the team

parts.note: XI is eleven, a cricket or football team

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word am is read upwards

parts.note: taken as written
a centaur is a mythical half-man, half-horse

explanation.surface: A skilled rider in the side announces that he is a rising star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising star' reads as a promising newcomer, but star alone is the definition. In a down clue 'rising' turns a word upwards; the team is a cricket eleven written in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: Proxima Centauri is the star nearest to the Sun, a red dwarf in the Alpha Centauri system.

clue.text: Free a Swede perhaps cornered by lion

indicators.note: the lion encloses the other pieces, trapping them

parts.note: Leo is the lion of the zodiac
a swede is a root vegetable, so veg

explanation.surface: A Swedish person gets free after being trapped by a lion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swede' suggests a person from Sweden; it is the root vegetable (rutabaga in America).
explanation.definitionFit: To leave go is a colloquial phrase meaning to release one's hold, letting something free.

clue.text: Smart dwarf, losing heart, pens a last letter

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so the shortened name wraps round the other pieces
the two middle letters of the dwarf's name are dropped

parts.note: Sneezy is one of the seven dwarfs in Disney's Snow White
Z is the final letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A well-dressed dwarf, feeling low, writes one final letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing heart' drops EE from SNEEZY to leave SNZY, and 'pens' puts A and Z inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Snazzy is informal for stylish or smart in appearance, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Major reckoning it's shocking about royal crisis

indicators.note: the shocking word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a numbing experience is shocking or stunning
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is a royal cipher
a crunch is a critical moment, a crisis

explanation.surface: A big calculation shows how shocking the royal crisis is.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is the monarch's cipher, short for Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: Number-crunching is large-scale calculation, heavy reckoning done with figures.

clue.text: In New Zealand not a fashionable fine wine

indicators.note: new suggests the letters are made over into a new order
the word a is left out of Zealand

parts.note: in means fashionable
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A New Zealand wine that isn't fashionable, though it is fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Zealand' looks like a place; New signals the anagram of ZELAND (Zealand without one A, as 'not a' says) with IN and F.
explanation.definitionFit: Zinfandel is a red grape variety and the wine made from it, grown widely in California.

clue.text: Miss Woodhouse, upset, breaks your jaw

indicators.note: the reversed name breaks into the short form of your

parts.note: YR is a written abbreviation of your

indicators.note: in a down clue the name is turned upside down, reading backwards

parts.note: Emma Woodhouse is the heroine of Jane Austen's Emma

explanation.surface: An upset Emma Woodhouse punches someone in the jaw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jaw' is a verb here, meaning to chatter. 'upset' in a down clue turns the heroine's name upside down; 'breaks' puts it inside the written short form of your.
explanation.definitionFit: To jaw is to talk at length, and to yammer is to chatter or complain loudly.

clue.text: Hunted around SE African state

indicators.note: the country goes round the compass letters

parts.note: Chad is a country in north-central Africa

explanation.surface: Pursued round the south-east of an African country.
explanation.walkthrough: SE is the compass abbreviation for south-east, taken as printed.
explanation.definitionFit: Chased means pursued, the same as hunted down.

clue.text: Volley ball with endless ease

indicators.note: the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a salve eases pain, and to salve is to ease
O is round like a ball

explanation.surface: A tennis volley hit with effortless ease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Volley' could be a tennis shot, keeping with ball in the surface; it is a burst of gunfire. 'endless' drops the last letter of the ointment word.
explanation.definitionFit: A salvo is a simultaneous discharge of guns, a volley of fire.

clue.text: Relating to particular individual made him no different

indicators.note: made different means these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something concerning a certain person made him no different.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin phrase describes an argument directed at a particular person rather than at the point.

clue.text: Perhaps lament players getting the sack?

definitions.text: Perhaps lament players getting the sack?

parts.words: Perhaps lament players getting the sack?
parts.note: reads like workers being fired, but a lament is a mournful tune played on an instrument built around a leather bag, the sack

explanation.surface: Performers of a sad song, maybe, are being dismissed from their jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting the sack' suggests dismissal; here the sack is the instrument's bag, and a lament is a traditional Scottish pipe tune.
explanation.definitionFit: Players of the Highland instrument with a bag and drones perform laments, so they are lament players.

clue.text: Get round plug to fill centre of lever

indicators.note: the advert fills the space in the middle of the other piece
all but the first and last letters of the word lever

parts.note: an ad is a plug, a piece of advertising

explanation.surface: An instruction to stop a gap in the middle of a lever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre of' takes the middle three letters of lever, not just the middle letter; 'to fill' puts the advert inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: To evade a rule or a question is to get round it by dodging.

clue.text: Powerful steer from expert with a learner at wheel

parts.note: a buff is an enthusiast with expert knowledge
L is the learner sign on a British car
O is round like a wheel

explanation.surface: Driving advice from an instructor with a learner at the wheel of a powerful car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steer' in the surface is guidance from an expert, but in the definition it is a bovine animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A buffalo is a massive, strong bovine, loosely a powerful ox or steer.

clue.text: Old rally champion supplied touring runs with drink

indicators.note: the supply word travels round the runs

parts.note: fed means supplied with food
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
perry is an alcoholic drink made from pears

explanation.surface: A former rally driver was given a drink while on tour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rally champion' suggests motor sport; the rally is in tennis. Fred Perry was a British Wimbledon champion of the 1930s.
explanation.definitionFit: Fred Perry won Wimbledon three times in the 1930s, a past champion of tennis rallies.

clue.text: Find hidden meaning in last month's poetry

parts.note: DEC is short for December, the last month of the year
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: Interpreting poetry published in the previous month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last month' suggests the one just gone; it is December, last in the year.
explanation.definitionFit: To decode a message is to work out its concealed meaning.

clue.text: Lily pad spoiled with holes

indicators.note: spoiled letters are damaged and rearranged

explanation.surface: A lily pad is ruined by being full of holes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lily pad' reads as one thing; Lily is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The asphodel is a plant of the lily family, famous from Greek myth.

clue.text: Slight chance of crashing on this flight

definitions.text: Slight chance of crashing on this flight

parts.words: Slight chance of crashing on this flight
parts.note: reads as an air-safety worry, but crashing means falling asleep, which is hard on an overnight flight

explanation.surface: A nervous flyer is told there is little risk of the plane going down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashing' is slang for collapsing into sleep; passengers on an overnight flight get little rest and arrive bleary.
explanation.definitionFit: An overnight flight is named for the bloodshot look of passengers who could barely sleep on it.

clue.text: Rang Czechs housed in pairs regularly

indicators.note: take alternate pairs of letters, keeping every second pair

explanation.surface: Czech people living two by two kept ringing.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'Czechs housed' into pairs CZ EC HS HO US ED; dropping every other pair leaves EC, HO, ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Echoed means resounded or rang out again, as a voice does in a cave.

clue.text: American left to enter digits messes up locks

indicators.note: the first pieces go inside the word for digits

parts.note: toes are the digits of the foot
US is short for American, as in United States

explanation.surface: An American who left to enter some numbers makes a mess with security locks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digits' suggests numbers and 'locks' door fastenings; they are toes and hair.
explanation.definitionFit: To tousle is to make hair untidy, so it means to mess up someone's locks of hair.

clue.text: Easy chance to gain illegal access

parts.note: a tap-in is an easy scoring chance in football or golf
taken as written

explanation.surface: An easy opportunity to break in somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Easy chance' looks like part of the definition; it is the sporting tap-in.
explanation.definitionFit: To tap into a phone line or system is to get access to it, often illicitly.

clue.text: Blow landed in skirmish, appropriately

indicators.note: the letters are set down inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A punch was thrown in a skirmish, as was fitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow' looks like a punch; it is a setback.
explanation.definitionFit: A blow is an unlucky misfortune, and a mishap is just such a setback.

clue.text: Feed with soft kernel the minimum for squirrel?

indicators.note: the soft letter becomes the core, set in the middle of the other piece

parts.note: the least a squirrel would want is a single nut: I (one) and NUT
P is piano, the musical direction for soft

explanation.surface: A squirrel's minimum rations, with a soft centre.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the whimsical phrase for one nut, I plus NUT; P goes in its centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Input is what is fed into a system, and to input data is to feed it in.

clue.text: Bound to put an end to children's game

parts.note: to bound is to leap or hop
to scotch a rumour or plan is to put a stop to it

explanation.surface: A children's game that is sure to be stopped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to' reads as 'certain to'; Bound is the jump.
explanation.definitionFit: This playground game involves hopping through numbered squares chalked on the ground.

clue.text: One wouldn't give up place in Germany

definitions.meaning: a person who keeps having a go, persevering
An ancient city on the Moselle in western Germany

explanation.definitionFit: A trier is someone who keeps trying; Trier is also an old German city near Luxembourg.

clue.text: Energy evident in revised re-launch of Old Labour

indicators.note: the energy symbol is to be seen inside the rearranged word
the letters of re-launch are reworked into a new order

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Energy is apparent in a revamped relaunch of the traditional Labour Party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Labour' looks political; it is the labours of Hercules from myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Herculean means relating to Hercules and his twelve ancient labours, hence to an old labour; now also 'enormously hard'.

clue.text: One struggled with climber

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
vied means competed or struggled

explanation.surface: Someone who wrestled with a mountaineer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climber' suggests a mountaineer; it is a climbing plant, ivy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivied means overgrown with ivy, a climbing plant, so covered with a climber.

clue.text: Masseuse maybe bubbly-sounding and round

indicators.note: the word for bubbly is said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: fizzy drinks are bubbly
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A massage therapist who is bubbly and plump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bubbly-sounding' signals a homophone of FIZZY, written PHYSI, before round O.
explanation.definitionFit: A physio is a physiotherapist, whose work includes massage, so a masseuse is one example.

clue.text: Bank with railway lines of inferior quality

parts.note: Dogger Bank is a large sandbank in the North Sea
EL is an elevated railway, as in Chicago

explanation.surface: A riverbank beside railway lines that are poorly built.
explanation.walkthrough: 'railway lines' suggests tracks; the lines are verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Doggerel is badly written verse, comic or crude lines of poor quality.
